ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Don't Let Anger Be Your Boss

fullPassage:
Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life.

As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing. In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions. In your teen years, this part is still in development. The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity. At the same time, however, you may feel confused about who you are. You may also be more sensitive to unfairness. Furthermore, your body is flowing with hormones. This significantly affects your mood. The combination of these factors intensifies your strong emotions.

It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn't mean there is something wrong with you. Anger can sometimes be a useful tool. For example, an angry but open conversation can resolve a conflict between friends. The important thing is to manage your anger so that it does not turn into aggressive or violent behavior. This does not mean that you should stop yourself from feeling angry. Rather, you should express it in a productive way. Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings. This can help you to better understand your anger.

You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way. Remember: anger is a feeling, but behavior is a choice. The first step is recognizing the physical signs of anger. It is possible to recognize those signs in advance. They include an increased heart rate, a flushed face, and the clenching of your fists. When these things happen, take action to reduce your anger. For example, you could try taking a break to organize your thoughts or ending a conversation before it gets too intense.

In some cases, the strategies mentioned above may not be enough, so you may need to find proper coping skills for your personal situation. Without the right coping skills, you may find yourself becoming verbally or even physically aggressive. Explore various strategies to discover what is best for you, such as taking a walk, drawing a picture, or writing down things that come to your mind. You can also try to find possible solutions to a problem and then compare the advantages and disadvantages of each one. By developing problem-solving skills, you will learn that there are many ways to solve a problem without getting angry.

Anger is an emotion that we all experience. By managing your anger properly, you can be the boss of your feelings, not the other way around. This is an important step in finding your true self and taking control of your life.

questions.passage: It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn't mean there is something wrong with you. Anger can sometimes be a useful tool. For example, an angry but ①<u>open</u> conversation can resolve a conflict between friends. The important thing is ②<u>to manage</u> your anger so that it does not turn into ③<u>aggressive</u> or violent behavior. This does not mean that you should stop yourself from ④<u>feel</u> angry.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 때때로 화가 나는 것은 자연스러우며 그것은 당신에게 문제가 있다는 것을 뜻하지 않는다. 중요한 것은 당신의 화가 공격적이거나 폭력적인 행동으로 변하지 않도록 관리하는 것이다. 이는 당신이 화를 느끼는 것을 멈추어야 한다는 것을 의미하지 않는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① open: 형용사, conversation 수식. 정상.
✅ ② to manage: The important thing is to manage (주격보어 to부정사). 정상.
✅ ③ aggressive: 형용사, behavior 수식. 정상.
❌ ④ feel → feeling: stop ~ from ~ing 구문. from 뒤에 동명사 필요.
det.tip: stop A from ~ing: A가 ~하는 것을 막다 / prevent/keep/prohibit A from ~ing 동일 패턴

questions.passage: As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing. In your brain, there is a part that is ①<u>responsible</u> for solving problems and ②<u>controlling</u> your emotions. The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity. At the same time, however, you may feel ③<u>confusing</u> about who you are. You may also be more ④<u>sensitive</u> to unfairness.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 십 대로서, 당신의 뇌는 여전히 자라고 있다. 뇌에는 문제 해결과 감정 조절을 담당하는 부분이 있다. 뇌의 변화는 독립성, 사회적 참여, 창의성으로 이끈다. 그러나 동시에 당신이 누구인지에 대해 혼란스럽게 느낄지도 모른다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ① responsible: 적절
✅ ② ② controlling: 적절
❌ ③ ④ confusing: 어법 오류
✅ ④ ③ sensitive: 적절
det.tip: confused(혼란스러워하는, 감정 주체) vs confusing(혼란스럽게 하는, 감정 원인) / -ed: 감정 느끼는 사람 / -ing: 감정 유발하는 것

questions.passage: In some cases, the strategies ①<u>mentioned</u> above may not be enough, so you may need to find proper coping skills for your personal situation. Without the right coping skills, you may find yourself ②<u>becoming</u> verbally or even physically aggressive. Explore various strategies to discover ③<u>that</u> is best for you, such as taking a walk, drawing a picture, or ④<u>writing</u> down things that come to your mind.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 경우에는 위에 언급한 전략이 충분하지 않을 수 있으므로 적절한 대처 기술을 찾아야 할지도 모른다. 올바른 대처 기술이 없다면 언어적으로 혹은 신체적으로 공격적이 될 수 있다. 무엇이 당신에게 가장 좋은지 찾기 위해 다양한 전략을 탐구해라.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ③ mentioned: 적절
✅ ② ② becoming: 적절
❌ ③ ① that: 어법 오류
✅ ④ ④ writing: 적절
det.tip: what = the thing that (선행사 포함 관계대명사) / discover what is best: 무엇이 최선인지 발견하다 / that은 선행사 필요

questions.passage: You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially ①<u>appropriate</u> way. Remember: anger is a feeling, but behavior is a choice. The first step is recognizing the physical signs of anger. It is possible to recognize those signs in ②<u>advance</u>. They include an increased heart rate, a flushed face, and the clenching of your fists. When these things happen, take action to ③<u>increase</u> your anger. For example, you could try taking a break to ④<u>organize</u> your thoughts.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 사회적으로 적절한 방식으로 화를 다루는 법을 배워야 한다. 화의 신체적 징후를 미리 알아차릴 수 있다. 이러한 것들이 발생할 때 화를 ③줄이기 위해 조치를 취해라.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②④ 원문 그대로 적절.
❌ ③ increase(증가시키다) → 원문은 reduce(줄이다). 화를 '줄이기' 위해 조치를 취하라는 문맥. increase는 반대.
det.tip: reduce(줄이다) ↔ increase(증가시키다) / take action to reduce: 줄이기 위해 조치를 취하다

questions.passage: It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn't mean there is something wrong with you. Anger can sometimes be a useful tool. The important thing is to manage your anger so that it does not turn into ①<u>aggressive</u> or violent behavior. This does not mean that you should stop yourself from feeling angry. Rather, you should ②<u>suppress</u> it in a productive way. Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings. This can help you to better ③<u>understand</u> your anger. You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially ④<u>appropriate</u> way.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 화가 공격적이거나 폭력적인 행동으로 변하지 않도록 관리해야 한다. 화를 느끼는 것을 멈추라는 뜻이 아니라, 생산적인 방식으로 ②표현해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①③④ 원문 그대로 적절.
❌ ② suppress(억누르다) → 원문은 express(표현하다). 바로 앞에서 '멈추지 말라'고 했으므로 '억누르다'는 문맥과 모순. '표현하다'가 맞음.
⚠️ 함정: suppress는 '생산적인 방식으로 억누르다'가 그럴듯해 보이지만, 앞 문장에서 '멈추지 말라'고 했으므로 모순.
det.tip: express(표현하다) ↔ suppress(억누르다) / Rather는 대안 제시: 멈추지 말되 → 표현하라

questions.passage: As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing. In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions. In your teen years, this part is still in development. The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity. At the same time, however, you may feel confused about who you are. You may also be more sensitive to __________.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 뇌의 변화는 독립성, 사회적 참여, 창의성으로 이끈다. 그러나 동시에 누구인지 혼란스럽고, 불공정에 더욱 민감해질 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② unfairness: 원문 그대로. 십 대가 불공정에 민감해진다.
✅ ① certainty(확실성): 문맥과 무관.
❌ ③ popularity(인기): 민감성과 연결 약함.
❌ ④ discipline(규율): 가능해 보이나 원문과 다름.
det.tip: sensitive to unfairness: 불공정에 민감한 / unfair(불공정한) → unfairness(불공정)

questions.passage: It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn't mean there is something wrong with you. Anger can sometimes be a useful tool. For example, an angry but open conversation can resolve a conflict between friends. The important thing is to manage your anger so that it does not turn into aggressive or violent behavior. This does not mean that you should stop yourself from feeling angry. Rather, you should __________.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: ① avoid all conversations when angry
② express it in a productive way
④ let others handle your emotions

det.korean: 화를 멈추라는 뜻이 아니라, 오히려 생산적인 방식으로 표현해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② express it in a productive way: 원문 그대로. Rather(오히려) 뒤에 대안 제시.
❌ ① avoid all conversations: 대화 자체를 피하라는 것은 앞에서 '열린 대화로 갈등 해결' 가능하다고 한 것과 모순.
❌ ③ completely eliminate: 완전히 제거하라는 것은 '자연스러운 감정'이라 한 것과 모순.
❌ ④ let others handle: 타인에게 맡기라는 내용 없음.
det.tip: Rather: 오히려 (앞 내용 부정 후 대안 제시) / express in a productive way: 생산적으로 표현하다

questions.passage: You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way. Remember: anger is a feeling, but behavior is a choice. The first step is recognizing the physical signs of anger. It is possible to recognize those signs in advance. They include an increased heart rate, a flushed face, and the clenching of your fists.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: ① 화의 신체적 징후를 미리 알아차리는 것은 불가능하다.
③ 행동은 감정에 의해 결정되며 선택의 여지가 없다.
④ 화를 다루는 방법은 사회적 기준과 무관하다.
② 화의 징후에는 심박수 증가와 얼굴이 빨개지는 것이 포함된다.

det.korean: 화의 신체적 징후를 미리 알아차리는 것은 가능하다. 증가한 심박수, 빨개진 얼굴, 주먹 쥐기가 포함된다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 불가능 → 원문은 'possible(가능)'.
✅ ② 원문과 일치: increased heart rate, flushed face.
❌ ③ 선택 여지 없음 → 원문은 'behavior is a choice(행동은 선택)'.
❌ ④ 무관 → 원문은 'socially appropriate way(사회적으로 적절한)'.
det.tip: in advance: 미리 / behavior is a choice: 행동은 선택이다

questions.passage: Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life. As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing. In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions. In your teen years, this part is still in development.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: ③ 올바른 대처 기술이 없으면 공격적이 될 수 있다.
① 위에 언급한 전략은 모든 상황에서 충분하다.
② 대처 전략은 한 가지만 사용해야 한다.
④ 그림 그리기는 효과적인 대처 방법이 아니다.

det.korean: 올바른 대처 기술이 없다면 언어적으로 혹은 신체적으로 공격적이 될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 원문과 일치.
❌ ① 모든 상황에서 충분 → 원문은 'may not be enough(충분하지 않을 수 있다)'.
❌ ③ 한 가지만 → 원문은 'various strategies(다양한 전략)'.
❌ ④ 효과 없음 → 원문은 drawing a picture를 대처 방법의 예로 제시.
det.tip: verbally: 언어적으로 / physically: 신체적으로 / coping skills: 대처 기술

questions.passage: Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life. As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: ① 갑자기 화가 나서 문을 쾅 닫는 경우가 있다.
③ 어떤 사람들은 십 대의 화를 나쁜 태도 탓으로 돌린다.
② 이러한 감정은 단순히 일상 스트레스에서 비롯된다.
④ 십 대의 뇌는 여전히 성장하고 있다.

det.korean: 갑자기 화가 나서 문을 꽝 닫거나 눈을 치켜뜬다. 어떤 사람들은 태도가 나쁘다고 생각한다. 그러나 이러한 감정들은 단순히 일상 스트레스에서 오는 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②④ 원문과 일치.
❌ ③ '단순히 일상 스트레스에서 비롯된다' → 원문은 'don't simply come from stress'(단순히 스트레스에서 오는 것이 아니다). 부정문.
det.tip: don't simply come from: 단순히 ~에서 오는 것이 아니다 — 부정문을 긍정으로 바꾼 변조

questions.passage: It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn't mean there is something wrong with you. The important thing is to manage your anger so that it does not turn into aggressive or violent behavior. This does not mean that you should stop yourself from feeling angry. Rather, you should express it in a productive way. Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings. This can help you to better understand your anger.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: ④ 화를 생산적으로 표현하고 관리하는 것의 중요성
③ 십 대의 호르몬 변화와 뇌 발달

det.korean: 화를 관리하여 공격적 행동으로 변하지 않게 하되, 화를 멈추지 말고 생산적으로 표현하라.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 화를 생산적으로 표현하고 관리하는 것의 중요성: manage anger + express in a productive way.
❌ ① 완전히 없애기: 본문은 '멈추지 말라'고 함.
❌ ③ 갈등 피하기: 갈등 '해결'이지 '피하기'가 아님.
❌ ④ 호르몬/뇌: 이 단락의 주제가 아님.
det.tip: 주제문: manage anger + express productively = 화 관리와 생산적 표현

questions.passage: Anger is an emotion that we all experience. By managing your anger properly, you can be the boss of your feelings, not the other way around. This is an important step in finding your true self and taking control of your life. You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way. Remember: anger is a feeling, but behavior is a choice.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: ① 화는 통제할 수 없는 본능이므로 받아들여야 한다.
② 모든 감정은 나쁘므로 억제해야 한다.
③ 화를 적절히 다루면 삶의 주도권을 가질 수 있다.

det.korean: 화를 적절히 관리하면 감정의 주인이 되어 삶을 장악할 수 있다. 화는 감정이지만 행동은 선택이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 통제 불가: 본문은 '관리 가능(manage properly)'
✅ ② 화를 적절히 다루면 삶의 주도권을 가질 수 있다: be the boss of feelings + taking control of your life.
❌ ③ 모든 감정 억제: 본문은 화를 '멈추지 말라'고 함.
❌ ④ 감정>행동: 본문은 'behavior is a choice(행동은 선택)'로 행동의 중요성 강조.
det.tip: be the boss of your feelings: 감정의 주인이 되다 / behavior is a choice: 행동은 선택

questions.passage: Anger is an emotion that we all experience. By managing your anger properly, you can be the boss of your feelings, <u>not the other way around</u>. This is an important step in finding your true self and taking control of your life.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 <u>not the other way around</u>가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: ② 감정이 당신을 지배하는 것이 아니라는 것
③ 다른 사람의 감정을 이해하는 것

det.korean: 화를 적절히 다루면 당신이 감정의 주인이 될 수 있다. 그 반대가 아니라(화가 당신을 지배하는 것이 아니라).
det.analysis:
✅ ② '감정이 당신을 지배하는 것이 아니라': 'you can be the boss of your feelings'의 반대 = 감정이 당신의 boss가 되는 것.
❌ ① 화를 느끼지 않는 것: 본문은 '느끼는 것 자체를 멈추지 말라'고 함.
❌ ③ 다른 사람의 감정: 언급 없음.
❌ ④ 표현하지 않는 것: '생산적으로 표현하라'의 반대.
det.tip: not the other way around: 그 반대가 아니라 / the boss of feelings ↔ feelings being the boss of you

questions.passage: As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing. In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions. In your teen years, <u>this part</u> is still in development. The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity. At the same time, however, you may feel confused about who you are.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 <u>this part</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.passage: You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way. The first step is recognizing the physical signs of anger. It is possible to recognize those signs in advance. <u>They</u> include an increased heart rate, a flushed face, and the clenching of your fists. When these things happen, take action to reduce your anger.

det.analysis:

❌ ② 적절한 방식: 방식이 아니라 징후.

questions.passage: In some cases, the strategies mentioned above may not be enough, so you may need to find proper coping skills for your personal situation. Without the right coping skills, you may find yourself becoming verbally or even physically aggressive. Explore various strategies to discover what is best for you, such as taking a walk, drawing a picture, or writing down things that come to your mind. You can also try to find possible solutions to a problem and then compare the advantages and disadvantages of each one. By developing problem-solving skills, you will learn that there are many ways to solve a problem without getting angry. Anger is an emotion that we all experience. By managing your anger properly, you can be the boss of your feelings, not the other way around. This is an important step in finding your true self and taking control of your life.
